citations.assessment: The accessible Menachot text actually names Acha son of Rava, where he addresses Rav Ashi. The reference is relevant evidence for the competing patronym, not confirmation of bar Rav.
Rav Acha bar Rav exempts. Rav Mesharshya calls the exempting authority his father’s father.
The matching dispute has Rav Adda bar Natan, whereas Heilprin records Acha. Mar Zutra gives the opposing view; Rav Mesharshya invokes his grandfather’s view and the wolf analogy.
Rashi expressly identifies the grandfather as Rav Acha, in tension with the running text’s Adda bar Natan.
The inspected Asheri text has Rav Acha son of Rava in the lung dispute.
The running text has Rav Acha bar Yaakov. Its footnote records a different Gemara reading.

The accessible Rosh has bar Rava in the case narrative, and describes the early disputant as Rav’s son in the commentary. Its relative clause calls Mesharshya a student of Rava. Heilprin’s later quotation has Rav; its variant requires printed collation.
The cited entry explicitly refers back to the Rosh discussion and the Rav Acha bar Rav entry.
The linked entry presents competing reconstructions of the Eruvin 24a genealogy, including Rav as Rav Acha’s possible son and Mesharshya’s father.
The accessible text has Rav Acha son of Rava transmitting the dispute concerning an open-sided structure. It does not reproduce the reported Achi form or Ravina message.
